content: 1. Higginson IJ and colleagues conducted a systematic review to identify symptoms and concerns among children and young people with life-limiting and life-threatening conditions. Their study emphasized the importance of meaningful health outcomes in this population. (Patient, 2019; 12:15–55). 2. Afolabi O and colleagues reviewed clinical management guidelines for COVID-19 in African countries to assess their alignment with African quality palliative care standards. Their findings highlighted gaps in current guidelines. (J Pain Symptom Manage, 2021; 61:e17–23). 3. Namisango E and colleagues systematically reviewed symptoms, concerns, and health outcomes among children and young people with life-limiting and life-threatening conditions, emphasizing the need for person-centered care. (Patient, 2019; 12:15–55). 4. Frigati LJ and colleagues investigated chronic comorbidities in children and adolescents with perinatally acquired HIV in sub-Saharan Africa during the antiretroviral therapy era. Their findings revealed significant health challenges in this population. (Lancet Child Adolesc Health, 2020; 4:688–98). 5. Sleeman KE and colleagues projected the global burden of serious health-related suffering by 2060, analyzing data by world regions, age groups, and health conditions. Their study underscored the escalating need for palliative care. (Lancet Glob Health, 2019; 7:e883–92). 6. Smit M and colleagues modeled future challenges in clinical care for an aging population living with HIV, highlighting the complexities of managing comorbidities and long-term care needs. (Lancet Infect Dis, 2015; 15:810–8). 7. Croxford S and colleagues analyzed mortality and causes of death among people diagnosed with HIV in the era of highly active antiretroviral therapy, comparing outcomes with the general population. (Lancet Public Health, 2017; 2:e35–46). 8. Sohn AH and colleagues determined standardized causes of death among infants, children, and adolescents living with HIV in Asia, providing critical insights into mortality patterns in this population. (AIDS, 2020; 34:1527–37). 9. Gwyther L, Brennan F, and Harding R advocated for advancing palliative care as a fundamental human right, emphasizing its role in comprehensive healthcare. (J Pain Symptom Manage, 2009; 38:767–74). 10. Downing J and colleagues conducted a population-based street survey in Kenya to understand public preferences and priorities for end-of-life care, revealing cultural and societal influences on care decisions. (BMC Palliat Care, 2014; 13:4). 11. Powell RA and colleagues explored public priorities and preferences for end-of-life care in Namibia, identifying key factors influencing care delivery in resource-limited settings. (J Pain Symptom Manage, 2014; 47:620–30). 12. Gomes B and colleagues conducted a population survey across multiple European countries to examine preferences for the place of death among individuals with advanced cancer, providing valuable data for palliative care planning. (Ann Oncol, 2012; 23:2006–15). 13. Harding R and colleagues compared the place of death for people with HIV across eleven countries, using death certificate data to identify disparities in end-of-life care. (BMC Infect Dis, 2018; 18:55). 14. Harding R, Epiphaniou E, and Chidgey-Clark J systematically reviewed the needs, experiences, and preferences of sexual minorities for end-of-life and palliative care, highlighting significant gaps in care provision. (J Palliat Med, 2012; 15:602–11). 15. Bristowe K and colleagues provided recommendations to reduce inequalities in care for LGBT individuals facing advanced illness, based on a national qualitative interview study. (Palliat Med, 2018; 32:23–35). 16. Bristowe K, Marshall S, and Harding R reviewed the bereavement experiences of LGBT individuals who lost a partner, synthesizing themes and modeling the literature to inform supportive care strategies. (Palliat Med, 2016; 30:730–44). 17. Hunt J and colleagues conducted an in-depth qualitative study on accessing palliative care for key populations, revealing barriers such as isolation, discrimination, and lack of family support. (Palliat Med, 2019; 33:685–92). 18. Hunt J and colleagues explored the healthcare experiences of LGBTI individuals and sex workers in Zimbabwe, identifying stigma and discrimination as significant barriers to care. (BMJ Glob Health, 2017; 2:e000168). 19. Namisango E and colleagues conducted a multi-country qualitative study to identify self-reported symptoms, concerns, and priority outcomes among children with life-limiting illnesses, aiming to improve person-centered care. (Palliat Med, 2020; 34:319–35). 20. Harding R and colleagues systematically reviewed evidence on the impact of palliative care on outcomes for patients with HIV/AIDS, demonstrating its benefits in improving quality of life. (Sex Transm Infect, 2005; 81:5–14). 21. Lowther K and colleagues analyzed data from a mixed-methods trial to identify active ingredients of a person-centered intervention for people on HIV treatment, emphasizing the importance of tailored care. (BMC Infect Dis, 2018; 18:27). 22. Lowther K and colleagues evaluated the effect of participation in a randomized controlled trial of an integrated palliative care intervention on HIV-associated stigma, highlighting its potential to reduce stigma. (AIDS Care, 2018; 30:1180–8). 23. Lowther K and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial in Kenya to assess the impact of nurse-led palliative care for HIV-positive patients on antiretroviral therapy, demonstrating improved outcomes. (Lancet HIV, 2015; 2:e328–34). 24. Reid EA and colleagues systematically reviewed the cost-effectiveness of palliative care in lowand middle-income countries, providing evidence for its economic and clinical benefits. (BMJ Support Palliat Care, 2019; 9:120–9). 25. Desrosiers T and colleagues demonstrated that a hospital-based palliative care service for patients with advanced organ failure in sub-Saharan Africa reduced hospital admissions and increased home death rates. (J Pain Symptom Manage, 2014; 47:786–92). 26. Krakauer EL and colleagues emphasized the importance of integrating palliative care and pain control into primary healthcare to improve health outcomes and reduce poverty. (World Bank, 2017; 9:235–46). 27. WHO's Model List of Essential Medicines for Children (7th edition) provides a comprehensive guide to essential medications for pediatric care, emphasizing accessibility and equity. (Accessed 1 June 2021). 28. Singh E and colleagues reviewed HIV-associated malignancies in children, highlighting the need for early detection and tailored treatment strategies. (Curr Opin HIV AIDS, 2017; 12:77). 29. Bohlus J and colleagues analyzed the incidence of AIDS-defining and other cancers in HIV-positive children in South Africa, using record linkage to identify patterns and risk factors. (Pediatr Infect Dis J, 2016; 35:e164). 30. Simard EP and colleagues examined long-term cancer risk among individuals diagnosed with AIDS during childhood, providing insights into the need for ongoing surveillance and care. (Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev, 2012; 21:148–54).
